items.name: PNG
items.summary: PNG is a lossless raster format that reproduces every pixel exactly and fully supports transparency.
items.best_for: logos, icons, screenshots, and any graphic with sharp edges or a transparent background

technical.colorDepth: 1–16 bits per channel; truecolor, greyscale or 256-colour palette
technical.metadata: Text chunks, ICC profile, gamma; EXIF via the newer eXIf chunk
technical.typicalSize: Large for photos (often 2–3× a JPG); tiny for flat graphics
technical.support: Universal — every browser, OS and editor

items.name: JPG
items.summary: JPG is a lossy format tuned for photographs, trading a little detail for dramatically smaller files.
items.best_for: photographs and richly detailed images where a small file size matters most

technical.compression: Lossy (8×8 DCT blocks, quantisation, chroma subsampling)
technical.colorDepth: 8 bits per channel; RGB/YCbCr, greyscale or CMYK
technical.typicalSize: Smallest of the classic formats for photos
technical.support: Universal — every browser, camera and device

items.name: WebP
items.summary: WebP is a modern Google format offering both lossy and lossless modes, transparency, and files 25–35% smaller than JPG or PNG.
items.best_for: fast-loading website images that keep transparency and quality

technical.colorDepth: 8 bits per channel, RGB(A); lossy mode uses 4:2:0 chroma
technical.transparency: Alpha in both lossy and lossless modes
technical.typicalSize: Roughly 25–35% smaller than JPG/PNG at similar quality
technical.support: All modern browsers; most current editors and OSes

items.name: AVIF
items.summary: AVIF is a next-generation format built on the AV1 codec, producing the smallest files of any mainstream format at a given quality.
items.best_for: cutting-edge web delivery where the very smallest file size wins

technical.compression: Lossy or lossless (AV1 intra-frame in a HEIF container)
technical.colorDepth: 8, 10 or 12 bits per channel; HDR and wide gamut capable
technical.metadata: EXIF, XMP, ICC / CICP colour signalling
technical.typicalSize: Usually the smallest — often half a JPG at similar quality
technical.support: Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari 16+; patchy in older desktop software

items.name: GIF
items.summary: GIF is an older format limited to a 256-color palette, best known for short looping animations.

technical.compression: Lossless LZW, but limited to a 256-colour palette
technical.transparency: 1-bit (a pixel is fully transparent or fully opaque)
technical.typicalSize: Small for simple graphics; large and banded for photos

items.name: BMP
items.summary: BMP is an uncompressed raster format that stores raw pixel data, yielding large but universally readable files.
items.best_for: maximum compatibility with legacy Windows software and raw, lossless pixels

technical.compression: Usually none (raw pixels); optional RLE for palette images
technical.support: Universal on Windows; opens almost everywhere

items.name: TIFF
items.summary: TIFF is a high-quality, typically lossless format favored in printing, scanning, and professional photography.
items.best_for: print production, scanning, and archival master files

technical.compression: None, LZW, ZIP (lossless) or JPEG (lossy) — chosen per file
technical.colorDepth: 8, 16 or 32 bits per channel; RGB, CMYK, Lab, greyscale
technical.metadata: Rich tags: EXIF, IPTC, XMP, ICC profile
technical.typicalSize: Large — uncompressed 8-bit RGB is about 3 bytes per pixel
technical.support: Print, scanning and pro editors; most browsers cannot display it

items.name: SVG
items.summary: SVG is a vector format that describes images with math, so it scales to any size while staying perfectly crisp.
items.best_for: logos, icons, and illustrations that must stay sharp at every size

technical.compression: Not applicable — XML text describing shapes (gzip as .svgz)
technical.metadata: Title, description and arbitrary XML metadata
technical.typicalSize: Tiny for logos and icons; grows with path complexity
technical.support: All browsers; vector editors such as Illustrator, Inkscape, Figma

items.name: ICO
items.summary: ICO is the Windows icon container that bundles one or more small images used for favicons and application icons.

technical.colorDepth: Up to 32-bit RGBA per embedded size
technical.typicalSize: Small — usually a few sizes from 16×16 to 256×256

items.name: HEIC
items.summary: HEIC is Apple's High Efficiency format and the iPhone default, storing photos at roughly half the size of JPEG.

technical.compression: Lossy HEVC (H.265) intra-frame in a HEIF container
technical.colorDepth: 8 or 10 bits per channel; Display P3 on iPhone
technical.animation: Live Photos and bursts are stored as sequences
technical.metadata: EXIF, XMP, depth maps, HDR gain maps
technical.typicalSize: About half a JPG of the same photo
technical.support: Apple devices natively; Windows needs an extension; most browsers cannot display it

items.name: PSD
items.summary: PSD is Adobe Photoshop's native format, storing a flattened composite plus editable layers, masks, and effects.
items.best_for: layered editing in Photoshop and design hand-off

technical.colorDepth: 8, 16 or 32 bits per channel; RGB, CMYK, Lab, greyscale
technical.metadata: XMP, EXIF, ICC profile, guides, layer names
technical.typicalSize: Very large — layers multiply the size
technical.support: Photoshop, plus Photopea, GIMP and Affinity (partially)

items.name: TGA
items.summary: TGA (Targa) is a simple lossless raster format with an optional alpha channel, long used in games and video production.
items.best_for: game textures, sprites, and video pipelines that need lossless alpha

technical.metadata: Optional image ID and extension area
technical.typicalSize: Large — close to raw pixel size
technical.support: Game engines, 3D and video tools; browsers cannot display it

items.name: PPM
items.summary: PPM is a minimal, uncompressed Netpbm format that stores raw RGB values behind a tiny text header, easy for programs to read and write.
items.best_for: programming, image-processing pipelines, and academic use

technical.compression: None (raw binary P6 or ASCII P3)
technical.colorDepth: 8 or 16 bits per channel, RGB only
technical.metadata: Comment lines in the header only
technical.typicalSize: Very large — exactly width × height × 3 bytes plus a header
technical.support: Image-processing libraries, Netpbm, GIMP; not browsers
